boxBlock.note: Step_0:732-762. Anchor verified unique in the file (grep -cF == 1) and the slice taken by ifStatementEnd is brace-balanced (line 762 closes it). The chain self-selects on rr AND difficulty: rr 1 -> (viewX+320, viewY+200); rr 5 -> +237 (cut); rr 7 -> +200 with maxxscale 2 / maxyscale 1.5; rr 9 -> +200 and, only at difficulty 1, maxxscale 1.5 / maxyscale 2; everything else -> +170. obj_growtangle's own defaults are maxxscale = maxyscale = 2 (gml_Object_obj_growtangle_Create_0.gml:13-14). DO NOT try to extend this slice with an endAnchor at the scr_moveheart line: Step_0:769 is the closing brace of the enclosing `if (rtimer == 0 && attackdone == 0)`, so any slice reaching line 770 carries a stray `}`. DO NOT move the anchor up to `if (rtimer == 0 && attackdone == 0)` (Step_0:720) to capture more: that block calls event_user(0), which is the CHOOSER, and would re-roll the attack out from under the studio - the exact trap already recorded for the Knight.

boxBlockWineHide.note: Applies to types 2 / 2.1 / 2.2 only, and must be injected as a literal (not grepped): it sits after the closing brace of the box block, and its own `if (rr == 2)` line is NOT unique in the file (3 hits: Step_0:332 and :997 are dialogue). The only unique substring inside it is `obj_growtangle.sprite_index = spr_nothing;` (1 hit, Step_0:766). The Wine turn also skips the boss's own scr_moveheart (Step_0:771 guards on `rr != 2`); the controller places obj_heartmarker and calls scr_moveheart itself once the glass has been thrown (obj_queen_bulletcontroller_Step_0.gml:373-382).

turnBlockNote: Queen has NO separate turn-length ladder. Every scr_turntimer call lives INSIDE its own `case` of the switch at Step_0:783-981, interleaved with the scr_bulletspawner calls, so there is no slice that sets the turn length without also re-spawning the controller (the Knight double-spawn trap). Use `dispatchBlock` (replay the whole switch instead of spawning) or `turnByChoice` (hand-authored). Without one of them every Queen attack falls back to the studio floor and the long attacks - Wine 400, Ultimate 371 - are cut off at 90/120 frames.

dispatchBlock.note: Step_0:783-985. Both strings verified unique (grep -cF == 1 each; `switch (rr)` @783, `turns += 1;` @986). The whole switch self-selects on the boss's own rr + difficulty and carries every scr_turntimer call. Replay this INSTEAD of manually spawning a controller - it spawns one itself - never in addition.

chooser.note: event_user(0), 248 lines, called once per turn from Step_0:724-727 (`if (attackdebug < 0) event_user(0); else rr = attackdebug;`). It assigns BOTH rr and difficulty. attackdebug is -1 and difficultydebug is 0 in Create (Create_0.gml:17-18) and only the debug keypress handler changes them, so the chooser is always authoritative. Structure: forced-turn overrides (wine / ultimate, lines 5-45), then a phase-1/2 ladder+pool (47-132), then a phase-3/4 ladder+pool (134-242), then a berdlyplug fallback (244-248).

turnByChoice.note: Keys are `rr`, with `rr.difficulty` only where the case actually raises the value. Derived with scr_turntimer's raise-only semantics applied (gml_GlobalScript_scr_turntimer.gml: `if (global.turntimer < arg0) global.turntimer = arg0;`). Two consequences: (a) case 3's `scr_turntimer(190)` for difficulty 3 (Step_0:845) is a NO-OP — the unconditional `scr_turntimer(240)` at Step_0:834 already ran, so type 3.3 would get 240, not 190; (b) case 1's `scr_turntimer(311)` (Step_0:802) is dead because ultimateattackused is still 0 when the dispatcher runs — obj_queen_ultimate_attack_controller_Create_0.gml:8 only sets it to 1 afterwards, and the ultimate can fire at most once (see phases.ultimateOnce). `preAttackFloor` is the `else scr_turntimer(120)` at Step_0:1015, which runs on every frame with rtimer 1..15; it can never override a case value. global.turntimer counts down to 0 each turn (obj_battlecontroller_Step_0.gml:1075-1077), so each turn starts from 0 and the raise-only rule applies per turn.

phases.phaseturnNote: phaseturn is NEVER reset on a phase change — Create_0.gml:28 is its only initialiser. The phase-1/2 branch clamps it to 7 (Other_10.gml:91-93) and then rolls its pool; the phase-3/4 branch does NOT clamp, so it climbs through the 8..12 ladder and then into its own pool. Because there is no reset, a player who reaches phase 3 early carries a low phaseturn and replays the early ladder, while a player who ground out phase 1-2 enters phase 3 at phaseturn 7 and jumps straight to the phaseturn-8 arm (rr 4 d1). Wine and Ultimate turns each do `phaseturn -= 1` so they do not consume a ladder slot.

mechanics: Four HP/mercy-gated phases driving a per-phase-turn ladder plus a random pool (obj_queen_enemy Other_10 = event_user(0)). rr picks the attack, difficulty picks the sub-type, and both come out of the same ladder arm — Queen never randomises difficulty independently. Red soul only: no green, blue, purple or yellow mode anywhere in the fight. Two turns are not ordinary bullet turns. (a) WINE (rr 2) hides the battle box entirely (Step_0:764-768 sets obj_growtangle.sprite_index = spr_nothing and visible = false) and suppresses the boss's own scr_moveheart (Step_0:771 guards on `rr != 2`). Queen throws her glass through a three-state animation (wineglasscon 1 -> 2 -> 3, Step_0:96-165) and only at the end of wineglasscon 3 does she do `with (obj_queen_bulletcontroller) init = 3;` (Step_0:156-157); the CONTROLLER then destroys any obj_heartmarker, places a new one at obj_growtangle.x - 8 / y + 30 and calls scr_moveheart itself (obj_queen_bulletcontroller_Step_0.gml:373-382). The turn is then 'tilt the giant glass, catch the falling acid droplets'; difficulty 1/2 add a sinusoidal glass rotation (`obj_queen_wineglass.image_angle = sin(ctimer / turnperiod) * turnamount`, :447-451). (b) ULTIMATE (rr 1, type 1) creates obj_queen_ultimate_attack_controller and covers the real soul with obj_hiddenheart (obj_queen_bulletcontroller_Step_0.gml:339-343); it is a scripted joke turn — fade out the heroes, a download progress bar, obj_queen_poppup_error popups and obj_queen_explodinghead_intro passes — not a bullet pattern. The ACID SHIELD (obj_queenshield_enemy) is created indirectly when obj_queen_wineglass is destroyed at the end of a wine turn (obj_queen_wineglass_Destroy_0.gml:4 -> obj_queenshield_intro, which spawns the shield at winetimer == 23). While it exists the ACT menu swaps Loosen -> Toast and GroupLoosen -> GroupToast and drops Throw (Other_11.gml, which re-runs scr_spellmenu_setup); Toasts drain shieldacthp, and the shield also bleeds 10% of shieldmaxhp per turn (Step_0:294-298). obj_berdlyplug_enemy is a permanent second on-field object (Berdly wired into the ceiling): it is the mercy target for the Loosen/GroupLoosen/Throw ACTs (Step_0:1060-1075, :1173-1188, :1273-1288, :1370-1385, each `bardlymercy += mercyset` followed by `with (obj_berdlyplug_enemy) event_user(0)`), it is physically pulled by BerdlyTornado (obj_queen_bulletcontroller_Step_0.gml:952 sets obj_berdlyplug_enemy.con = 1) and by the Throw ACT, which spawns an aiming minigame, obj_queen_throw_controller (Step_0:1236-1241, only while no shield exists). Queen is monstertype 48: HP/maxHP 1510, AT 10, DF 0, mercymax 100 (scr_monstersetup.gml:1345-1394). Encounter 59 (scr_encountersetup.gml:585-603).
engineNeeds: 1) SWITCH DISPATCH — Queen is the first boss whose dispatcher is a `switch (rr)` (Step_0:783-981) rather than an if/else chain. gen_attacks.js's attackAnnouncements() cannot handle it: walking backward from an announcement to the enclosing `{` lands on the switch's own opening brace, so `setup` comes out as either the entire switch (>3500 chars, then nulled) or every preceding case; and the `<var> == N)` back-scan for the branch value finds `if (rtimer == 16)` at Step_0:781 and would record selector 'rtimer', choice 16 for EVERY Queen attack. The forward window also runs past each case's `break` into later cases, over-collecting extraFields (bufferattack/damage/target). Fix with a switch-aware slicer (case label -> next case label) or hand-authored setups from the line ranges above. 2) NO TURN LADDER — turnBlock is null; use dispatchBlock or turnByChoice.
